idiom_name: goroutine + buffered result channel (or a callback function the worker invokes)
implementation_notes: Go replaces the classic start-method/completion-event structure with a goroutine and a channel: the function starts the work in the background and returns a channel that will carry exactly one result - or accepts a callback function the worker calls later - and the receiver takes it when ready, honouring 'do not communicate by sharing memory; instead, share memory by communicating'. context.Context takes the place of the cancellation flag, select adds timeouts and fan-in for free, and no operation object with progress/cancel members is built. Use the callback form only where exposing a channel would leak an implementation detail across an API boundary.
pitfalls: An unbuffered one-shot result channel with no receiver leaks the goroutine forever - buffer size 1 (or a select on ctx.Done()) is the safe default for a single result.
Closing the result channel from the receiver, or twice, panics; a single-result channel is usually not closed at all and must never be closed by the consumer.
A callback invoked by the worker runs on a foreign goroutine: shared state must be handed over by value or protected, or the race detector will find it.
